# Step 6: Facets

## Introduction

Add the limits that let okb check your data: [fixed values](../../../../../docs/GLOSSARY.md#concept-fixed-value), [defaults](../../../../../docs/GLOSSARY.md#concept-default-value) and [inverse slots](../../../../../docs/GLOSSARY.md#concept-inverse-slots).

You want every wine's body to be light, medium or full, never "pretty strong". A [facet](../../../../../docs/GLOSSARY.md#concept-facet) is how you say that. You already set several in step 5, with `--values`, `--card` and `--min`. This step adds the rest. You can read the full guide to this step in [Method](../../../../../docs/METHOD.md#step-6-facets).

## What you'll make

Facts that hold for a whole class, a default value, a link between `maker` and `produces`, and one pairing with a strength. The `validate` command now has more to check.

## Run the commands

First, join the two slots from step 5. They describe one fact from two sides, so make them [inverses](../../../../../docs/GLOSSARY.md#concept-inverse-slots) and okb stores the fact once:

```bash
okb relationship inverse maker produces
```

```text
maker and produces are now inverses: one relationship read from both ends.
Stored as (Wine)-[:MAKER]->(Winery); produces follows MAKER backwards, so nothing is stored twice.
```

Next, set the [fixed values](../../../../../docs/GLOSSARY.md#concept-fixed-value). Every red wine is red, every dessert wine is sweet, and red wine goes with red meat. State each one once, on the class:

```bash
okb class fix RedWine color=red
okb class fix WhiteWine color=white
okb class fix RoseWine color=rose
okb class fix DessertWine sugar=sweet
okb class fix RedWine goesWellWith=RedMeat
okb class fix WhiteWine goesWellWith=Seafood
```

```text
RedWine.color fixed to "red"
Fixed values apply to every subclass and instance and can't be changed below. For an overridable starting value use `okb class default`.

WhiteWine.color fixed to "white"

RoseWine.color fixed to "rose"

DessertWine.sugar fixed to "sweet"

RedWine.goesWellWith fixed to RedMeat

WhiteWine.goesWellWith fixed to Seafood
```

How good a pairing is belongs to the pairing itself, not to the wine or the food. A property on a link is called an [edge property](../../../../../docs/GLOSSARY.md#concept-edge-property). Add a `strength` to `goesWellWith`, then record that red wine with red meat is a classic:

```bash
okb relationship property goesWellWith strength --type Enumerated --values classic,good
okb link RedWine goesWellWith RedMeat strength=classic
```

```text
goesWellWith edges can now carry strength (Enumerated): (…)-[:GOES_WELL_WITH {strength: …}]->(…)

Updated (RedWine)-[:GOES_WELL_WITH {strength: "classic"}]->(RedMeat)
```

Last, a [default](../../../../../docs/GLOSSARY.md#concept-default-value). Most wines are medium-bodied, so set that once. A wine can still say something different:

```bash
okb class default Wine body=medium
```

```text
New Wine instances will start with body = "medium" (can be changed per instance).
```

## Read the output

- **[Fixed versus default](../../../../../docs/learn/facets.md).** A fixed value can't change: no red wine is white. A default is a starting guess that any wine can override.
- **Facts about classes.** `goesWellWith=RedMeat` is on the class, so it covers every red wine, including ones you add later.
- **Why strength is an edge property.** "Classic" isn't true of red wine or of red meat. It's true of the pairing. Run `okb explain decision.edge-or-class` to see how okb helps you choose.

## Check your work

Run the checks again. Facets are where okb catches most data-quality errors:

```bash
okb validate
okb status
```

```text
✗ 0 error(s)   ! 1 warning(s)   i 2 hint(s)   · checks for steps 1–6 (use --all for the rest)

WARNINGS: fix, or record a design decision explaining why not
  ! 'Merlot' doesn't add anything to 'RedWine': no own slots, values, restrictions or relationships. [hier-subclass-adds-something]
      Fix: Add the slot, value, restriction or relationship that makes it different; or mark it
      `terminological`; or merge it into its parent.

HINTS: worth a look
  i The subclasses of 'RedWine' ('Bordeaux', 'Beaujolais', 'Merlot', 'Port') have no disjointness declared. Can anything be more than one of them? [disjoint-consider-siblings]
      Fix: `okb class disjoint A B C`, or ignore it if the siblings can overlap (Dessert Wine
      and White Wine can).
  i The subclasses of 'Medoc' ('Pauillac', 'Margaux') have no disjointness declared. Can anything be more than one of them? [disjoint-consider-siblings]
      Fix: `okb class disjoint A B C`, or ignore it if the siblings can overlap (Dessert Wine
      and White Wine can).

EXPLAINED by design decisions (2)

  · 'Bordeaux' has only one direct subclass ('Medoc'). Is a sibling missing, or is the subclass really the same as its parent? [hier-single-child] → d.3

Learn about any rule: okb explain <rule-id>   ·   add --why for reasons and sources
(6 warning(s)/hint(s) from later steps are hidden until you get there; okb validate --all shows them. Errors are never hidden.)

Step 6 looks done. When you're happy with it: okb step next
```

`validate` shows one warning: Merlot "doesn't add anything" to RedWine. That's fair, because it has no slots or values of its own yet. You'll fix it in step 7, when Merlot gets its grape. The step is done even so, because a warning isn't an error. When step 6 has a tick, move on:

```bash
okb step next
```

```text
Now on step 7. (To read a step's guide without moving: okb explain 7)

Step 7 of 8: Create instances

  Goal: Add real individuals: choose a class, create the instance, and fill in its slot values.
  Why it matters: Instances are the real test. Filling them in shows up missing slots, wrong
  facets and classes that don't fit.

Questions to answer
  • What are the most specific things that appear in answers to your competency questions? Those
  are your instances.
  • Which class does each belong to? (The most specific one that fits.)
  • Can you fill in every required slot? If not, is the data missing or is the facet wrong?

You're done when
  ○ At least a few instances (enough to answer one competency question end to end)
  ○ The instances have no known mistakes

Tips
  • Start with instances that answer one competency question completely. It's the fastest way to
  find gaps.
  • An instance that won't fit anywhere usually means a class is missing or a facet is too
  strict.

In Ontology 101's wine example
  • Château Morgon Beaujolais is an instance of Beaujolais, with:
  • body light, color red, flavor delicate, tannin low
  • grape Gamay, maker Château Morgon, region Beaujolais, sugar dry

Decision guides for this step  (okb explain <id>)
  decision.instance-or-class   Instance or class?

Commands
  okb instance add   okb instance set
```

> **Common mistakes**
>
> - **Fixing a value that has exceptions.** If some red wines are really pink, a fixed `color=red` is wrong. Use a default.
> - **Storing both directions.** Joining `maker` and `produces` with `inverse` means you only ever write one of them.
> - **Putting the strength on the wine.** A wine has many pairings, and each one has its own strength.

## Next step

You set fixed values, a default, an inverse and a strength on a pairing. Next, you'll add real wines and wineries to test the model.
